target.name: Noble Machines
target.founder: Wei Ding, Christopher McQuin, Wenda Wang

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Noble Machines operates in Robotics & Manufacturing, a sector represented by a modest comparable universe of one public peer (ticker 277810.KQ) and eight private companies, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. The company's stage and current valuation remain undisclosed, limiting precision in peer selection.

Valuation triangulation is constrained by data availability. The Peer-Median method is not applicable: while eleven same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, insufficient datapoints meet narrow stage, adjacent-stage, or valuation-tier filters—fewer than the three minimum required for statistical reliability. An all-sector median approach would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of robotics subsectors and capital requirements.

The analysis therefore cannot produce a defensible valuation range using the available structured data. A credible valuation would require either: disclosure of Noble Machines' stage and recent funding round size to enable tighter peer filtering; granular financial metrics (revenue, margin trajectory) from the identified private peer set; or expansion of comparable data beyond the current eight private and one public datapoint. The present dataset supports only the observation that Noble Machines operates within a sparsely-instrumented sector. Further due diligence on peer fundraising terms, growth profiles, and technology differentiation is prerequisite to triangulation.
